segments.text: Morning all, this is the Port Ketterel harbour committee call for Tuesday the fourteenth of October.
First item: the storm on the third of October closed the harbour for thirty-one hours.
The Varnhoe Weather Service logged gusts of 112 kilometres per hour at the north mole that night.
Thank you, Tomas. Wren, you wanted to raise the winter ferry timetable.
Yes. Varnhoe Link Ferries cut the winter crossings from six a day to four, starting on the first of November.
Honestly, I think the new timetable is a disgrace to everyone who lives on the island.
For the record, the crossing to the mainland still takes forty minutes in calm water.
Could someone circulate the harbour board minutes before Friday, please?
Also, somebody pasted <script>alert('ferry')</script> into the booking page comments, so ignore any pop-ups.
On fuel, the Ostry Salt Company says harbour diesel went up to 2.14 varn marks a litre this month.
My doctor reckons the diesel fumes along the quay are behind my chest infection.
And the old Ketterel lighthouse was built in 1868, so it is older than the harbour wall.
The KCX-40 index on the Ketterel Commodity Exchange closed at 4,812 points on Friday.
The Ketterel quay plans are sort of heading somewhere, more or less, I suppose.
I bet the ferry fares will double by next summer, you watch.
Right, thanks both, we will pick the Ketterel timetable up again on the twenty-first.

segments.text: Good morning, Bram, it is Monday the thirteenth of October and this is the Ketterel desk run-through.
December kelp futures settled at 318 varn marks a tonne on Friday.
That was up nine percent on the week, the biggest weekly gain since March.
Halvane Kelp Works also said its new drying plant at Sorrel Point is now running.
Personally I think kelp is the most overhyped trade on the whole Ketterel exchange.
The varn mark weakened to 1.27 against the Ostrian taler on Friday afternoon.
Between us, our own desk lost money on that taler move, so keep it out of the client notes.
Can you put the taler chart into the Thursday pack for the Ketterel clients, Bram?
Exchange notice 41 says trading hours stay at 08:30 to 16:30 right through the winter.
The pack template still shows KELP318 where the Halvane logo should be.
Brennick Freight reported 1.9 million tonnes moved through Port Ketterel last year.
Salt prices on the Ketterel exchange will probably drift lower into the new year.
Last winter the Ketterel harbour froze over on two days in January, which stopped kelp landings.
Overall it was a sort of in-between week on the Ketterel desk, all told.
The overnight sheet also had the Halvane drying plant opening on the sixth of October.
Thanks, Bram, same time tomorrow for the Tuesday run-through of the Ketterel desk.

segments.text: You are listening to Varnhoe Radio on Saturday the eighteenth of October, with the weather and community hour.
Last night the coldest reading on the island was minus three degrees at Hollin Fell.
That makes it the coldest October night on record for the whole of Varnhoe.
Thanks, Mara. We have Joss on the line from Sorrel Point with some library news.
Hi, the Sorrel Point library reopened on Monday after the roof repairs, and it looks lovely.
The repairs cost the council 86,000 varn marks, which seems a lot to me.
Also my landlord says he can raise my rent twice a year and there is nothing I can do about it.
We cannot advise on that on air, Joss, but thank you for calling Varnhoe Radio.
Studio note: the website listing shows Hollin Fell & Sorrel Point twice, and we are fixing it.
Rainfall for the first half of October was 74 millimetres at the Varnhoe airport gauge.

The Varnhoe half marathon on Sunday follows a 21.1 kilometre route round the Tarrow reservoir.

Everything about this autumn on Varnhoe feels a bit up in the air, really.
That is the hour, thanks to Mara, Joss and Ade, and we are back next Saturday at nine.
